# Instructor guide · Topic 8: Queue & Deque

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Use queues for first-come-first-served processing, know why collections.deque beats list.pop(0), and use circular buffers and monotonic deques.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **FIFO: first in, first out:** A queue adds at the rear and removes from the front, like a line at a shop.
- **Why list.pop(0) is a trap:** A list stores items side by side, so removing the first one shifts all the others.
- **Queues in practice:** Queues model anything processed in arrival order: requests, events within a time window, simulations, and breadth-first search.
- **Circular queue:** A fixed-size array where the rear wraps around to index 0.
- **Monotonic deque: sliding window maximum:** Keep a deque of indexes whose values decrease.

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **41 minutes** of guided material (5 lessons)
- Practice: 9 coding problems and 30 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 7 (Stack)

Open the topic in the browser (`#t/queue`) and project it; every lesson alternates a short explanation with questions the class answers together.

## Live coding demonstrations

- Code the first “Code it” problem of each lesson live, thinking aloud.
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Sliding Window Maximum: max of every window → monotonic deque** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Queue and deque · Circular queue · Sliding window maximum (monotonic deque)

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- Queue order?
- Python queue?
- Cost of list.pop(0)?
- deque weakness?
- Circular queue next slot?
- Window max trick?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Number of Recent Calls (`q-recent-counter`)
- Moving Average (`q-moving-avg`)
- Stack Using a Queue (`q-stack-from-queue`)

Code tracing on the board: Both ends of a deque (`q-p1`), rotate (`q-p2`), A deque with maxlen (`q-p3`), First in, first out (`q-p4`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: A queue that is a stack (`q-d1`), Rear of a circular queue (`q-d2`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Find the Winner of the Circular Game (`q-josephus`)
- First Negative in Every Window (`q-first-negative`)
- Build from scratch: Build a Queue (`build-queue`), Build a Circular Queue (`build-circular-queue`)

## Homework

- Reveal Cards in Increasing Order (`q-reveal-cards`)
- Sliding Window Maximum (`q-window-max`)
- Finish the topic's Review quiz in the browser and clear the revision queue.
